name: Negotiate and execute the prime contract
summary: When an owner awards a bid or proposal, the company has to turn it into a signed prime contract, usually a CCDC 2 stipulated price contract or a CCDC construction management or P3 agreement, within the short deadline in the award letter. The project manager reconciles the bid with the contract documents, contracts counsel compares the contract with the tendered terms and negotiates any changes through the vice-president of business development, treasury obtains the performance and payment bonds, the risk manager the insurance certificates, and authorised officers sign. Unacceptable risk terms, owners who will not change tendered clauses, slow sureties and missing documents delay signing for weeks.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B of annual construction revenue, an Ontario head office and regional offices in Western and Atlantic Canada, bidding public and private institutional, commercial and industrial buildings.
baseline.notes: CCDC 2 2008 was still common in 2019-2020 and CCDC 2 2020 spread from 2021; digital bonds and electronic signatures became usual during 2020-2021.

trigger: A public, private or P3 owner issues a letter of award or intent after the company's bid or proposal is selected.
end_state: Both parties have signed the prime contract and it is handed to project startup, or the award falls through.

volume.seasonality: More awards from May to August, after the spring tender season.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate tied to project starts (7-10-14 a month).

surge.cause: late spring and summer awards after the spring public tender season

evidence.note: Follows the organisation file surge on stipulated bids with a lag of one to two months for bid validity and owner approvals.

steps.name: Receive the award notice
steps.description: The business development manager receives the owner's letter of award or intent, reads the conditions and deadlines (usually bonds, insurance and signed documents within about ten days), and confirms receipt to the owner.

error.defect_description: A deadline in the award letter is overlooked.

evidence.note: Letter of award binds the contractor; documents due within 10 days of award.

steps.name: Update the CRM and announce the award
steps.description: The business development manager marks the opportunity as awarded in the CRM with the contract value, moves it into pending backlog, and emails operations, finance and estimating.

error.defect_description: Contract value keyed wrongly in the backlog report.

evidence.note: Awarded but not yet contracted work is tracked as pending backlog; times are estimates.

steps.name: Assign the project manager
steps.description: The regional vice-president names the project manager and superintendent for the job, considering who is coming free, and books an award meeting with estimating.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; regional VPs staff projects in the organisation file.

steps.name: Reconcile the bid with the contract documents
steps.description: The project manager reads the bid summary, bid form, addenda, accepted alternates and separate prices against the contract documents the owner sends, and lists every difference in scope, price or schedule.

error.defect_description: An accepted alternate or a post-bid clarification is left out of the contract sum.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; bid-to-contract reconciliation.

steps.name: Explain the bid to the project manager
steps.description: The lead estimator walks the project manager through the bid summary, carried trades, plugs, allowances and risks, so that the contract and later buyout reflect what was priced.

error.defect_description: A plug or exclusion is not explained.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; the organisation file lists estimators in ops-project-startup, not here.

steps.name: Review the draft contract against the tender terms
steps.description: Contracts counsel compares the agreement, supplementary conditions, insurance, bonding and payment terms in the contract the owner issued with the terms tendered, and flags changes and risk terms such as consequential damages, unlimited liquidated damages and broad indemnities.

error.defect_description: A changed clause is not spotted.

control.basis: Company contract review policy: counsel reviews every prime contract before signature

next.condition: contract matches the tender; no material issues

evidence.note: CCDC 2 2020 terms (indemnity limited to direct loss, supplementary conditions that need updating); share is an estimate.

steps.name: Draft the exceptions and positions
steps.description: Contracts counsel writes a mark-up of the clauses the company wants changed or clarified, with a fallback position for each, and circulates it to the project manager and vice-president.

error.defect_description: Mark-up made on an outdated draft.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; red-line mark-ups.

steps.name: Agree the negotiation positions
steps.description: The vice-president of business development meets the regional vice-president, project manager and counsel to decide which changes must be won, which can be priced, and how far to push an owner who tendered fixed terms.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; the organisation file names vp-bd as contract lead.

steps.name: Send comments and meet the owner
steps.description: The vice-president sends the mark-up and scope reconciliation to the owner and meets the owner, consultant and owner's counsel to negotiate the clauses, the contract sum and the schedule.

evidence.note: Owners may negotiate scope with the low bidder within the tender framework; times are estimates.

steps.name: Owner responds to the comments
steps.description: The owner and its lawyer consider the mark-up and reply with an accepted, partly accepted or rejected version; public owners often refuse changes to tendered terms.

next.condition: no agreement; award withdrawn or declined

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; share of second rounds and failures; a bidder that refuses to sign forfeits its bid security (oshawa).

steps.name: Approve the final terms
steps.description: The regional vice-president reviews the agreed contract, the remaining risk terms and the reconciled contract sum and approves signing within the regional delegation, or sends it up to the chief operating officer.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for contract signature by value and risk

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; delegation limits.

steps.name: Executive approval of non-standard terms
steps.description: The chief operating officer reviews the contract terms outside policy, such as uncapped liability or unusual liquidated damages, with the general counsel's note and approves or sends the team back to the owner.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: COO approves prime contracts with terms outside policy

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed for this process; the COO takes part in exec-bid-approval in the organisation file.

steps.name: Request the performance and payment bonds
steps.description: The treasury, surety and credit manager sends the surety broker the contract price, owner and bond forms required, usually a 50% performance bond and a 50% labour and material payment bond, and confirms the surety's approval within the bonding line.

error.defect_description: Bond request shows a contract price before reconciliation changes.

control.basis: Owner bonding requirements on award (Oshawa: 50% performance and 50% labour and material bonds) and, for Ontario public contracts of $500,000 or more, the Construction Act mandatory bonds

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed for this process; bond amounts and timing from the sources.

steps.name: Surety issues the final bonds
steps.description: The surety underwrites the final bonds against the agreement to bond given at tender, and the broker issues the performance bond and labour and material payment bond, in digital or paper form.

evidence.note: Bonds on award from the surety that gave the agreement to bond; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Arrange the insurance certificates
steps.description: The risk and insurance manager checks the contract's insurance clauses (general liability, builder's risk or wrap-up, limits, additional insureds) against the company program and asks the broker for certificates naming the owner and consultant.

error.defect_description: An additional insured or a project-specific limit is missed.

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed for this process; CCDC 2 2020 ties insurance to Ready-for-Takeover; times are estimates.

steps.name: Broker issues the certificates
steps.description: The insurance broker issues certificates of insurance and any builder's risk or wrap-up binder for the project and emails them to the risk manager.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; the wait runs alongside bond issue.

steps.name: Assemble the contract execution package
steps.description: The assistant project manager collects the bonds, insurance certificates, WSIB clearance certificate from the government portal, safety certification (COR), schedule of values and preliminary schedule into the package the award letter requires.

error.defect_description: A required document is missing or out of date.

control.basis: Workers' compensation clearance before work starts and owner's safety certification requirement (Nova Scotia guidelines 6.8; Oshawa COR rule)

evidence.note: Organisation file role not listed for this process; WSIB/WCB clearance and COR are named in the sources.

steps.name: Check the package against the award conditions
steps.description: The project manager ticks each item in the award letter and contract against the package, checks the contract sum on the agreement against the reconciliation, and returns missing items to the assistant.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; share of incomplete packages.

steps.name: Route the contract for signature
steps.description: Contracts counsel checks the signing authority matrix, prepares the execution copies with two signature blocks and routes them to the authorised officers.

control.basis: Corporate signing authority: two authorised officers sign prime contracts

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; two-signature rule.

steps.name: Officers sign the contract
steps.description: The chief operating officer and a second authorised officer sign the agreement, often electronically by 2021, after a final look at the contract sum and approvals.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; officer signature.

steps.name: Deliver the signed contract and securities
steps.description: The project manager sends the signed agreement, bonds, insurance certificates and clearances to the owner or consultant, by courier or upload, before the deadline in the award letter.

evidence.note: Contract documents and security due within 10 days of award.

steps.name: Owner executes the contract
steps.description: The owner checks the bonds and insurance, verifies digital bonds with the authentication service, and signs; public owners may need a board or council resolution or a second signing officer.

next.condition: owner cancels before signing (funding or scope)

evidence.note: Owner verifies bonds; council or other authority approval can be needed; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Close the award and hand over to startup
steps.description: The business development manager files the executed contract, marks the opportunity won with the final contract sum in the CRM, and sends the contract to project startup, finance for job set-up and risk for insurance records.

error.defect_description: Final contract sum differs from the CRM value.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; the organisation file sends the contract to ops-project-startup, preconstruction, design management and insurance.

exceptions.name: Second round of negotiation
exceptions.description: The owner rejects part of the mark-up and counsel redrafts; a third round happens on private and P3 contracts.

exceptions.name: Non-standard terms escalated
exceptions.description: Uncapped liability, unusual liquidated damages or very large contracts go to the COO before signature.

exceptions.name: Incomplete execution package
exceptions.description: A certificate or clearance is missing or expired and is chased before the package goes to the owner.

exceptions.name: Early start on a letter of intent
exceptions.description: The owner lets the company mobilise on a letter of intent while the contract is still being signed; startup runs in parallel with this process.

exceptions.name: Award falls through
exceptions.description: The parties cannot agree terms, or the owner cancels for funding or scope before signing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from award notice to executed contract
benchmarks.population: Canadian public and private building contracts

evidence.note: Author's estimate: public award letters ask for bonds and documents within about 10 days (ns2017, oshawa), then owners sign; negotiated private and P3 contracts take longer.

benchmarks.population: Nova Scotia public sector construction contracts; City of Oshawa bids

pain_points.description: Owners issue contracts with supplementary conditions that differ from or add to the tendered terms, and negotiation rounds wait on the owner's lawyers.

evidence.note: Supplementary conditions written for older CCDC forms need updating.

pain_points.description: Bonds, insurance certificates and clearances come from three outside parties against a ten-day deadline.

evidence.note: Ten-day deadline for contract documents and security.

pain_points.description: Scope agreed after bid (alternates, clarifications) is lost between the bid file and the contract sum.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor contracting practice; bid-to-contract handover.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Public Sector Construction Contract Guidelines (June 2017)
sources.supports: Prequalification of bidders with a published minimum score (often 70-80 of 100); solicitation documents list major subcontractors, bid security, CCDC contract form; bonding recommended at $500,000 and over; subcontracts of $250,000 or more should carry contract security; addenda no later than 5 business days (major) or 3 business days (minor) before closing and closing extended at least 1 business day when needed; late bids rejected; amendments and withdrawals allowed up to closing; withdrawal after opening only for serious demonstrable error within 2 business days; within 48 hours of opening bidders may be asked for safety certifications, other subcontractors and price breakouts; bids over the estimate may be negotiated or re-tendered; letter of award binds the contractor to sign; contract security within 10 days of award; bid security of unsuccessful bidders returned within 30 days; international trade agreements may require 40-day postings.

sources.title: Bid Submission Procedure (under Purchasing By-law 80-2020)
sources.supports: Electronic bids only through the bids&tenders system, late bids not accepted; COR, SOSE or ISO 45001 required for construction bids over $500,000; digital bid bond of 10% of the bid and agreement to bond uploaded with the bid on CCDC forms, verified through a third-party authentication firm; qualified bids, unverifiable bonds and improperly executed agreements to bond are rejected; contract documents due within 10 calendar days after written notice of award; acceptance time limit usually 90 days; performance bond of 100%, or 50% performance and 50% labour and material bonds, on award; only the low bidder's references checked; if the low bidder fails to execute, award to the next bidder and forfeit the deposit. PDF metadata shows the file was last saved in July 2021; the copy opened carries a later revision stamp.

sources.title: The new CCDC 2 - 2020: contract changes you need to know
sources.supports: CCDC 2 2020 keeps the delivery framework of the 2008 form; supplementary conditions written for 2008 may need updating; Ready-for-Takeover ends the Contract Time; monthly payment applications with workers' compensation evidence and CCDC 9A declarations; owner payment within 28 days; contractor responsible for health and safety (GC 9.4); indemnity limited to direct loss, no consequential damages (GC 13.1.2); insurance tied to Ready-for-Takeover.

sources.title: Bird Construction Inc. Announces 2021 Fourth Quarter and Annual Financial Results
sources.publisher: Bird Construction Inc. via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: 2021 new contract awards and change orders $2,540.0M against revenue $2,220.0M; backlog $3,002.5M and pending backlog $1,624.7M at year-end 2021; growth came despite timing delays in project tenders and awards from clients related to COVID-19; progressive design-build, IPD and alliance contracts.

assumptions: The process runs from the award notice to the executed contract; legal-prime-contract-review and fin-surety-bonding are separate processes, and their work for this contract appears here as the counsel and treasury steps.

Ontario's Construction Act mandatory bond rules (public contracts of $500,000 or more) are named in a control basis, but the statute could not be opened, so the evidence cites the City of Oshawa bond requirements instead.
Shares of negotiation rounds and failed awards are estimates; public stipulated tenders allow little negotiation, private negotiated and P3 contracts more.
Waits are calendar time; the main ones are the owner's legal review and execution, and the surety.

The organisation file lists only vp-bd, contracts-counsel, project-manager and regional-vp for this process; bd-manager, estimator, coo, treasury-manager, risk-insurance-manager and assistant-pm are added from the organisation file's roles.
No equipment, vehicles or crews are tied up; office roles have no shift pattern.
